blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Senate impeachment court is unlikely to grant Vice President Sara Duterte’s broad objections to the prosecution’s formal offer of evidence, Bicol Saro Rep. Terry Ridon said on Tuesday Ridon, an impeachment prosecutor, said Duterte’s lawyers virtually objected to all evidence presented by the prosecution concerning the unexplained wealth charge, including her net worth statements, bank records, tax documents and corporate filings. “I don’t believe the Senate impeachment court will uphold their blanket objection,” he told reporters in Filipino. “Sustaining it would mean no evidence whatsoever could be used in our trial, and I don’t think the Senate […]...
